How Much Does an AI Receptionist Cost for a Dental Practice?

Dental Automation

An AI receptionist for a dental practice typically involves several distinct cost components rather than one flat number: setup/configuration, a recurring monthly service fee, usage-based telephony and messaging costs, and any custom integration work. As a concrete reference point, 2S's Automate package — which includes AI receptionist setup — is priced from $999 setup + $399/mo.

Cost components, at a glance

These are the categories that typically make up the total cost. We don't publish invented industry-average dollar ranges for the usage-based and integration categories below, since actual costs vary by provider and practice — but here's what each one represents:

Cost Category What It Covers Typically Billed As
Setup / Configuration Configuring the assistant with your practice's information, booking rules, and approved answers; connecting it to your calendar or practice-management system; testing before launch. One-time
Monthly Service Hosting the assistant, ongoing maintenance, and platform access. Recurring monthly
Voice / Telephony Usage Actual phone call handling — minutes used, call routing, and any voice-specific provider fees. Usage-based
SMS / Messaging Usage Text messages sent and received through the assistant, billed by the messaging provider based on volume. Usage-based
Integrations / Custom Workflow Work Connecting to your specific practice-management software, CRM, or other systems beyond a standard setup, and building any non-standard workflow logic. One-time (varies by complexity)
Ongoing Changes / Support Adjusting the assistant's configuration as your practice's information, hours, or policies change after launch. Recurring monthly or as-needed

What the setup fee typically covers

Setup work includes configuring the assistant with your practice's actual information — hours, accepted insurance, services, booking rules — connecting it to your calendar or practice-management system, defining what it's allowed to answer, and testing it before it goes live. Practices with more complex scheduling or multiple locations generally involve more setup work than a single-location general practice.

What the monthly fee typically covers

The recurring fee generally covers hosting the assistant, ongoing maintenance, and support for adjustments as your practice's information changes. Usage-based costs — phone minutes, text messages, and similar telephony or messaging fees — are commonly billed separately by the underlying provider based on actual call and message volume, rather than bundled into a flat rate. Any such costs should be explained to you clearly before implementation begins.

What affects the price

  • Call and message volume the practice actually handles
  • Whether the practice needs voice (phone) capability, text-based capability, or both
  • Integration complexity — which calendar, CRM, or practice-management software it needs to connect to
  • How many distinct scenarios it needs to be configured to handle (scheduling, insurance questions, new patient intake, etc.)
  • Ongoing support and adjustment needs after launch

2S's approved pricing

2S's Automate package — which covers AI receptionist setup along with related workflow automation — is priced From $999 setup + $399/mo. This is a starting point, not a fixed quote; the exact cost for your practice depends on the factors above and is confirmed in a written proposal before any build work begins, with any third-party telephony or messaging costs disclosed at that stage.

A note on security and privacy

Any AI receptionist handling patient contact information should be configured with clear limits on what it can access and say, and a defined path for escalating anything sensitive to a person. This is a setup consideration to raise directly with whoever builds your system, not something to assume is handled by default. Applicable privacy and compliance requirements, the vendors involved, and how data flows between systems should be verified for your specific implementation rather than assumed.
